title: EGO 56V Combo Kit (47cm SP Mower + Trimmer + Blower + Rapid Charger + 5AH &  2.5AH Battery) $1,299 + $200 credit @ Total Tools
body:
Deal: EGO 56V Combo Kit (47cm SP Mower + Trimmer + Blower + Rapid Charger + 5AH &  2.5AH Battery) $1,299 + $200 credit @ Total Tools

[probablynotlauren] Anyone got one? I have a Ryobi 36V 46cm atm and it's 'fine' but want a bit of an upgrade to SP. This or a 36V SP Ryobi?
[Slippery Fish] Green works used to do a mower and snipper for $700, that is a fairly great kit
[Tj1987z] I've had two ego mowers currently own the steel deck, but if this is the polydeck, and self propelled you won't regret it.
I actually wish I didn't changeover.
[sunnymel] I have the same kit and some other ego tools. My only issue is the batteries never go on sale. They force you to buy more kits which includes batteries.
[axloz] I have an older version of this I bought about 4 or 5 years ago - mower, blower, battery kit. All still working wonderfully. I just used it again today actually!
I went for the ego mower because it has a plastic deck but it feels really solid to use and can take a beating. Plastic deck makes it nice and light to lug around.
[SentientControl] I've had the EGO 52cm Self-Propelled Mower & Multi-Tool w/ Line Trimmer Attachment since April this year. Came from an old Honda Petrol Mower. I love the EGO so easy, I now sort of enjoy mowing the lawn. The best thing is the trimmer and how it power loads the replacement cord without taking the reel off - so much easier, and Amazon sell the replacement cord.
[Solrak] I have the same Ego 52cm setup as you and love it. Now mowing isn't such a chore after all. I'm just waiting on a BF deal for a lawn edger to complete the kit.
[Banj0] Same here. Got an Ego 52cm coming from a Rover with B&S motor I bought 30 years ago. Beautiful cut, but the bigger deck is not quite as agile as the old petrol (I think it was about a 47cm). Gotten very comfortable with it now though, and almost enjoy mowing with it. No complaints about power…better than the old Briggs and Stratton, which was an upper-range domestic beast.
I'm skeptical that the Ego will last 30 years though. Still, I don't regret losing petrol outdoor tools (the mower was the last thing).
Wish Ego made a nice mulcher.
[2027] Been rocking the same stuff for about 5 years now. Came from a Honda too.
My first impression still reverberates, it’s light and easy to manoeuvre. It’s easy to use one handed, easy to get into tight places.
Now to the downsides. I never had to pull the Honda more than once to start. It was a pearler. Occasionally Ego will refuse to turn on, and it takes a few goes.
It does the trick, but it does stall easier than the Honda. That’s a fact.
Batteries are wearing out much quicker than I hoped. I’ve gone thorough 3x 7.5ah in 5 years. Not cheap. I’m actually seriously considering buying a battery tab spot welder gizmo and some cells next time a battery craps itself.
Replacement blade has gone from $45 in 2023 to $69 these days. WTAF.
If the Honda got clogged with wet grass and stalled, I could pull the cord slowly to dislodge the grass. Ego has no such function, gotta tip it and give it a reach around. Also, the handles won’t go parallel to the ground, say good bye to getting under a big trampoline easily.
Warranty service is great, I had some broken bits and batteries within a year of purchase, they had parts out to me nice and quick.
Trimmer on the other hand is nothing but praise. I love it. I can hold it in such a way that if it were my old Honda trimmer, the exhaust would be in my ear, and I find it easy to do the edging like that.
5 years in, it was not a cost saving measure. Anyone thinking that, forget about it. Batteries are tipping the equation.
Would I buy it again with all this in mind? Yes. And I wish that my neighbours would too…
Interestingly, Honda do have electric steel deck mowers now… I’m tempted.
[schquid] 100% agree on the batteries. Best advice is to absolutely flog them during the warranty period and if they start showing any sign of being weird ("overheating" quickly, jumping from near full to empty quickly, charger indicating they're fully charged when they aren't etc) get them replaced.
I have one great 5Ah battery that can outlast the other 3 5Ah combined, but mine started acting up a bit after the warranty ran out.
[alphalpha] Yep same experience on the batteries. Had 2 that came in a bundle and both now misbehaving. Won't charge or power tools. Both 3years, 7 months and EGO won't replace them as they are 7 months out of warranty. Be very wary of EGO batteries going forward. I have Aldi and Ozito batteries that are cheaper and still going
[Rillanon] interesting i have 2x2.5ah and 1x9ah and now coming up to 5 years, I hope they don't die.
[ribbon] Missed that deal, kinda regret now, hope to see the 52cm come up on Black Friday deals
[Rillanon] how do people load the strings, i use the auto load button and i always have one end slightly longer than the other end and have to chop it off. what a waste
[Frackingiscool] Honestly if they havn't already paid for the rights to the Skyhooks song for all future advertising they have missed a huge opportunity.
[cornflakes] God damn, I went down a rabbit hole last night with trimmers/brushcutters.
Currently using a corded '1200W' Ryobi and an old school 2 stroke Ryobi Scrub Hornet on 2 acres.
I was looking to grab a Stihl FS91 or Honda with the GX35, but after some reading found that the 40cm Ego one can match the power of the petrol ones - can someone confirm this for me? All roughly the same price, give or take.
I was looking at the ST1624E-T - with auto feeding line and a carbon shaft. Would imagine it's heaps lighter than petrol ones. I quite like the instant power delivery and torque of my corded one, but extension cords are a pain.
On occasion I do need to brushcut some thick bush shit, which I imagine the FS91 would eat through easily. Wonder how the Ego would go?
[TooSerious2] You're a glutton for punishment using a cord on 2 acres. Don't overthink it. I have Stihl electric for about 2 acres amid bush. Stihl is probably overpriced. Future you will thank you
[Mungulz] Have a look at the Ozito 36v, the brushless $269 one with the black head. Comes with a slashing attachment which might be useful for you. Seems plenty powerful.
Downsides, heavy, weird shaft orientation imo.
[Tommohalby] Throwing in that cap made the deal! I'm in
[mickeyjuiceman] It's a good cap, you're right there. Like all their gear, really.
[doggmatic] Awesome deal I have this stuff about 4 years old now still going strong
[Skad832] Brought this kit last week when it was on 10% off and used it today, one of the best buy ever!!
Two battery combo 5.0ah and 2.5ah with the rapid charger is sufficient for 500sqm lawn with thick over grow buffalo.
It has all the bells and whistles for general domestic use.
Coming from hopeless Ozito lawnmover and trimmer, huge difference!!
Money well spent!!
[sboy] Hi mate, I'm in similar boat. I've ozito 36v steel deck mower. It's kind of good but not sure if it's really worth the upgrade. Were u using the 36v ozito or 18v.
Plz suggest.
Thanx
[Wiser] Make sure you are not charging the battery when it is warm.
Whick kills the battery sooner
[fireball99] The tools are good.
The first gen mower is still going but the line trimmer died after 12yrs.
The batteries are shit I've got a pile of dead ego batteries 2.5ah, x2 4ah , 5ah , 7.5ah on the way out.
I did buy the new tab less 8ah battery and it is amazing lasting way longer than the 7.5ah even when it was new.
Basically giving up the cost of tool maintenance and servicing for battery cost.
[ruprectaus] their ride on on special ?
EDIT: I see they are but the ZTE I want is not, they only have the old school one that needs both hands on it to operate, I have a few trees to go under and hold branches away etc
[Skad832] Mate, this is wayyyy better than Ozito day and night difference. I had Ozito 36v, 410mm plastic deck.
Ozito got no power and will always struggle, this one powers through without any sweat. With Ozito I will easily burn 4 x 5.0ah batteries, Ego will use 2/3rd of 1x5.0ah battery. Fast charger will charge whole battery within minutes unlike Ozito's hours.
The real reason why I had to buy another mover is because mine Ozito lawnmover wheel broke in June, I placed order through special orders in July they say I will probably receive in December. Now I have 5x 5ah batteries with a broken lawnmover.
Hope helps
[Crowing] For those that bought the discounted ultimate gift cards today at office works, total tools is a retailer and seems like can redeem multiple gift cards per purchase. So extra 10% off.
I’m moving into a house with relatively small patch of grass in the front as well as the council strip. Not sure if I should fork out $1200 for this set or spend ~$700 for Ozito…
[rumblytangara] A small patch of grass and a council strip? 56V 12K mower sounds a bit ott.
[Serpeant] I know electric mowers have more torque, but can they scalp to dirt like a petrol mower ?
[2027] LM2135SPE here with 7.5ah battery and shitty kikuyu grass - no. Well mostly no. It will cope if you inch it back and forth, actual move it a few cm forward and back and take all year, but nothing compared to my old GCV160 Honda. I used that Honda to literally move piles of dirt (actually digging with it, into the bag lmao) no way this thing can do that.
I do wanna revisit it with the new 8ah “max” batteries, they give higher current flow than my 7.5ah (and the 10ah) which is what the electric motor needs to prevent stalling.
Edit: Sydney Tools are offering $100 worth of points with the 8ah battery, I’ve ordered it, will soon know if it does the job
[2027] https://sydneytools.com.au/product/ego-ba4480x-power-80ah-ar…
Thanks to @fireball99 mentioning them here I didn’t even know they existed.
And from Ego about it:
https://blog.egopowerplus.com.au/2026/06/26/the-new-ego-arc-…
About to watch some YouTube videos, I hope they validate my purchase decision…
[fireball99] @2027: the 8ah is still quite new for me but it ran longer than a 7.5ah and 2.5ah combined whippersnipping . it doesnt seem to help my 1st gen lm2001e mower as it will still cut out in slightly thicker grass bcos i think the electric motor is just too weak
[ttt888] Description does not match the picture on the site? It talks about multi tool ….
[lilyesp] Yeh just thinming of buying electric mkwer
This vs ryobi 36v one?
Or should i just go with petrol cheap cheetah one
I like convenience of battery but if it gets stuck all the time and power low then itll be problematic
[mrgeckoz] Given my own experience with EGO vs. Ryobi Brushless Range, plus the reviews I have read, I honestly don't think the price premium for EGO is really worths it.
YMMV.
[Musing Outloud] I have gone fully in on Ego gear. The 56 volt batteries were what sold me.
I got a double deal 2 years back with the 52cm mower, 5 AH battery and blower, plus a multi head device with a 5 AH (line trimmer, edger, hedger, and small chainsaw branch trimmer).
I use these on my property, 1000m2 (600m2 of grass) and my MIL's property 600m2 (350m2 of grass), both with mostly tough old buffalo and some kikuyu.
I always had asthma and allergies but dont suffer anywhere near as badly having upgraded from a base model 4 stroke Victa and 240v ryobi trimmer and 240v ryobi hedger. My allergies can't cope with 2 stroke oil fumes.
I run the batteries down in use and only recharge them as I need before use. Lithium generally prefers that. I've not had problems with them after 2 years. The mower is light & easy to lift into the back of my wife's Suzuki S Cross.
The Ego mower has more guts than the old Victa, and the multitool's hedger and trimmer are better than the 240v ryobi's, but it does go through Ego branded trimmer line quite quickly on the buffalo. This is a buffalo issue not an Ego kit issue.
Hope this feedback helps.
[OzBargaincreeper] 10/10 skin design
4/10 battery longevity
100% should of gone ozito instead.
Owned Ego 42cm mower, blower and trimmer for over 5 years
[Rillanon] I have everything in this combo but bought separtely over the years, plus an extra charger + 2.5ah battery, got the blower for free via redemption.
[Wiser] Anyone still using the ones from Masters on the way out?
